doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

chapter: The Bay Area scene and tastes
title: Asian and Filipino influence in Bay Area music
summary: Asian jazz festival, and Filipino pianists Flip Nunez and George Mirabis.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Is there an Asian influence in the music here?
Yeah, oh yeah. There’s, of course we’re on the edge of the Pacific you know.

There are, in fact there’s an Asian festival here, a jazz festival, and there are musicians. I haven’t played with that many. It’s more sort of avante garde, and I’m just a straight ahead spang-a-lang. And that’s another thing. You just can — I do what I do. And I appreciate all kinds of music but I do what I do, I’m just not going to spread myself that thin and try to do everything just to say I could do it.

But there was a musician that, he passed a few years ago, a great, great pianist named Flip Nunez, a Filipino. And I used to work a lot with him and he was really good, played with Jon Hendricks and a lot of different people around here in the sixties and seventies. And then there was another one, a Filipino musician I played a lot with named George Mirabis, another pianist, a great musician. So there is of course Latin musicians, a lot of big Latin musicians, so it’s pretty diverse around here.
